title: Minimum Number of Operations to Make Arrays Similar
statement:
You get two arrays of positive integers, `nums` and `target`, of equal length. A move picks two different indices `i` and `j`, adds 2 to `nums[i]` and takes 2 away from `nums[j]`.

Call two arrays similar when each value occurs the same number of times in both, so only the multiset matters, not the order. Return the smallest number of moves that makes `nums` similar to `target`. The inputs guarantee that this can always be done.
constraints: nums can always be made similar to target
notes:
## Intuition

A move never changes whether a value is odd or even, and it never changes the array's total. So every odd value of `nums` must end up as an odd value of `target`, and every even value as an even one. Within each parity group, matching the smallest with the smallest, the second smallest with the second smallest, and so on, makes the total distance as small as possible (crossing two matches never shortens them).

Once each value has a partner, the gaps add up to zero overall. Every move closes 2 units of upward gap and 2 units of downward gap at once, so it removes 4 from the sum of absolute gaps. The answer is that sum divided by 4.

## Approach

1. Sort both arrays with one comparator: even values first, odd values after, and ascending inside each group. Because both arrays hold the same number of odd values, index `i` now pairs equal parities in sorted order.
2. Add `Math.abs(nums[i] - target[i])` to `totalGap` for every index.
3. Return `totalGap / 4`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [8, 12, 6]` sorts to `[6, 8, 12]` and `target = [2, 14, 10]` sorts to `[2, 10, 14]` (all even). The gaps are `4`, `2` and `2`, so `totalGap = 8` and the answer is `8 / 4 = 2`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log n) for the two sorts; the scan is O(n).
- Space: O(1) beyond the sort.

## Pitfalls

- Sorting by value alone pairs an odd value with an even one, which no sequence of moves can fix.
- Dividing by 2 counts each move twice: one move fixes 2 units upward and 2 units downward.
- On LeetCode the sum reaches about 10^11, so Java and C need a 64-bit total.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `byParityThenValue` | comparator: evens before odds, then ascending |
| `i` | index that pairs `nums[i]` with `target[i]` |
| `totalGap` | sum of absolute differences over all pairs |

narration.2: Order values by parity first (evens, then odds) and by size inside each group.
narration.3: Sort nums so its evens and odds each sit in ascending order.
narration.4: Sort target the same way; equal odd counts make index i pair equal parities.
narration.5: The total distance the values must travel starts at zero.
narration.7: Add how far nums[i] is from its partner target[i].
narration.9: Each move closes 4 units of total distance (2 up and 2 down), so divide by 4.
